speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status Epilepticus (or prolonged focal impaired awareness seizure mimicking absence). The patient is a 7-year-old with recurrent 3-4 minute episodes of staring, facial grimacing, post-ictal confusion, and an "aura" of a muddy taste. The duration (3-4 minutes) and post-ictal state are atypical for simple absence seizures (which last seconds without confusion) and suggest focal seizures or prolonged absence status.

REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram) - specifically looking for focal onset vs generalized 3-Hz spike-wave.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain.

What specific activities or triggers (e.g., flashing lights, stress, lack of sleep) seem to precede these episodes?
